item.title: Trump Shelters Flavio Bolsonaro, Risking Tensions With Brazil
item.description: The US decision to allow the defeated right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro to seek refuge in the US poses a fresh irritant to a bilateral relationship that has been marked by finger-pointing and accusations between the two countries’ leaders.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin

item.title: Rep. Moore: Congress Faces Packed Post-Midterm Agenda
item.description: Rep. Blake Moore (R-UT) says candidates need to be candid with voters about higher energy prices and the challenges driving them. Rep. Moore says Congress should take up bipartisan permitting reform after the midterms as lawmakers look for ways to address energy costs. Rep. Moore says reconciliation also needs to be addressed despite a packed lame-duck agenda that includes defense authorization and appropriations. Rep. Moore says any reconciliation package would likely change from earlier drafts and could include legislation he says would save hundreds of billions of dollars by targeting fraud. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Thomas: Alaska Controversy Could Shift Senate Race
item.description: John Thomas, Nestpoint managing director and veteran Republican pollster and Strategist, says the controversy surrounding another Dan Sullivan on Alaska's Senate ballot could materially affect a race within the margin of error by undermining voter trust. Thomas says Republicans can be difficult for pollsters to reach and that some close races could break differently than current polling suggests. Thomas says Vivek Ramaswamy's controversial Ohio ad was in poor taste and hurt Republicans on the ticket, while predicting Ken Paxton will narrowly win in Texas. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fox News Viewer Dip Before Election May Signal Republican Unease
item.description: Fox News, the most-watched cable news network, saw a 28% prime-time viewer decline over the past four weeks leading up to the midterm elections, a sign the network’s traditionally conservative audience may be less enthused about the Nov. 3 contest.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Miller

item.title: Stevenson Says Fed Is Waiting to See Economy Slow
item.description: Betsey Stevenson, Professor of Public Policy and Economics at the University of Michigan's Ford School and former Chief Economist of the Department of Labor, says the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged is puzzling because another increase is still likely. Stevenson says policymakers may be waiting to see whether the economy slows further before raising rates again. Stevenson says uncertainty around the midterm elections and potential changes in fiscal policy could also affect how high rates ultimately need to go. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Alphabet, MSFT Earnings (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Charles Schwab is expanding its push into artificial intelligence, bringing Anthropic’s Claude for Financial Advisors directly into Schwab Advisor Center. The company says it is the first RIA custodian to offer Anthropic’s advisor-specific AI to independent firms. Alison Dooher, Head of AI at Schwab Advisor Services, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Live from Schwab IMPACT Summit in Boston to discuss how AI is changing the financial advice landscape.
On today's episode:
Ed Ludlow, Bloomberg Tech Host Anurag Rana, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Tech Analyst Omar Aguilar, CEO & CIO of Schwab Asset Management Lisa Salvi, Head of Business Consulting & Education at Charles Schwab (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Vance Reached Out to Iran to Offer Medical Supplies
item.description: President Donald Trump acknowledged that Vice President JD Vance wrote to Iranian authorities, but downplayed the significance of his outreach, saying it was focused on offering medical supplies to the country.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Josh Wingrove

item.title: Private Jet Firm Used by Bolsonaro Had Sparked Scandal for Milei
item.description: The private jet in which Flavio Bolsonaro and his family traveled to Miami is operated by a company embroiled in a corruption scandal that ensnared Argentine President Javier Milei.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias and Patrick Gillespie

item.title: The Web of Investigations Flávio Bolsonaro Is Facing in Brazil
item.description: Brazilian conservative senator Flávio Bolsonaro is drawing heightened political and financial scrutiny after his dramatic escape to Miami following his defeat in Sunday’s presidential election to leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Gamarski, Matheus Piovesana and Daniel Carvalho

item.title: Big Take: The Uniquely American Experience of Redrawing Political Maps
item.description: A gamble on re-districting ahead of the US midterm elections may not pay off for Republicans, who redrew more than a dozen congressional districts across the country hoping to pick up more seats in Congress. Bloomberg's Josh Wingrove joins David Gura on the Big Take podcast to explain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Plays Down Concerns Over AI Financing, Fed Rate Policy
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he and his team are keeping tabs on the state of financing for the artificial intelligence build-out, and played down recent signs of concern.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy

item.title: House and Senate Races Investors Are Watching: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg journalists answer your questions about the midterm races Wall Street is watching in a Live Q&A on Friday, Oct. 30 at 10:45 a.m. EDT.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Hager, Steven Dennis, Michael MacKenzie and Catherine Lucey

item.title: CNN Adds Air Force One Access to Suit Over Trump White House Ban
item.description: CNN, MS NOW and Politico have revised their lawsuit against the Trump administration over press access to the White House to include a request for a court order to allow their journalists into other areas, including the Oval Office and Air Force One.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Trump Delays Robotics, Machinery Tariffs in Favor of More Talks
item.description: President Donald Trump said he would hold off on imposing tariffs on imports of robotics, industrial machinery and related parts and components, instead directing officials to hold talks with trading partners on those goods.
item.dc:creator: Laura Curtis

item.title: Trump-Backed John Sununu Pitches Independence in New Hampshire Senate Race
item.description: A member of the state’s political dynasty has become more explicit about distancing himself from the unpopular leader of his party.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ryan

item.title: Fed Says More Data Will Help Next Decision as It Holds Rates: Fed Special
item.description: Bloomberg's Tom Keene, Jonathan Ferro and Lisa Abramowicz discuss remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh after the Federal Reserve decided to hold interest rates steady. Warsh told reporters that more information would help the FOMC make it next decision and repeated his vow to get inflation down and deliver price stability, 'no ifs, ands or buts.' Warsh also revealed that the FOMC would phase in an adjusted meeting schedule, voting at seven of its eight meetings next year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New Zealand Opportunity Party’s Wong Vies With Winston Peters for Kingmaker Role
item.description: Qiulae Wong’s rapid ascent could make her the power broker for the next government.
item.dc:creator: Ainsley Thomson

item.title: Trump Calls for Peltola to Be Banned From Alaska Senate Race
item.description: President Donald Trump intensified his attacks on Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola following a report that her allies secretly recruited candidates, including one with a similar name to Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, to join the state’s Senate race.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: A New Spanish Tragedy Forces a Pre-Election Political Reckoning
item.description: Antonio Hidalgo was on the sixth car of a commuter train bound for Seville on Wednesday morning, when about 118 kilometers (73 miles) south of Madrid, it collided with another train stopped on the track.
item.dc:creator: Clara Hernanz Lizarraga, Laura Millan, Daniel Basteiro and Macarena Muñoz

item.title: Bolsonaro Arrives in Miami With Family After Fleeing Brazil
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro landed in the US on Wednesday after fleeing Brazil, threatening to add new strains to relations between Brasilia and Washington and raising questions about his family’s future as a force on the Brazilian right.
item.dc:creator: Augusta Saraiva, Anna J Kaiser and Daniel Carvalho
